newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher - markets don't expect EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher - markets don't expect EMU delay.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Thursday he did not think the Bundesbank's dispute with Bonn would lead financial markets to take the view that European monetary union would be postponed.

Kuehbacher told German television network n-tv in an interview that the dispute between the central bank and Bonn over the valuation of gold and currency reserves demonstrated the government's determination to meet all EMU entry criteria.
That would allow Bonn to have a stronger say in the choice of European Union members joining monetary union at its planned start on January 1, 1999.
"I do not think that markets after this process have the impression that the euro will be postponed," Kuehbacher said.

He said the Bundesbank and the Bonn government took different views on the matter and noted that Finance Minister Theo Waigel must acknowledge that the bank's central council was unanimous in criticising his plan to boost the value of the bank's gold and currency reserves.
He also said the dispute was intensified by the fact that it coincided with planned amendments to Bundesbank legislation in preparation for European monetary union.
Kuehbacher also said he believed Waigel had been ill-advised in bringing forward legislation regarding the revaluation of Bundesbank reserves.
